scope: Bounded official evidence for Rio Pisco overflow and fluvial-erosion outcomes in Humay during 2023-2024, plus official Letrayoc hydrologic-monitoring and ANA current critical-point context. San Andres canal/coastal mechanisms are explicitly separated and are not treated as Rio Pisco outcomes.

confirmed_positive_outcomes.outcome: COEN-INDECI reports that rainfall in the upper basin increased Rio Pisco flow and the river overflowed, inundating agricultural land in Cuchilla Vieja.
COEN-INDECI reports intense rainfall followed by increased Rio Pisco flow and overflow, damaging transport infrastructure and agricultural production in Cuchilla Nueva.
COEN-INDECI reports increased Rio Pisco flow and subsequent overflow at El Palmar and Cuchilla Vieja, with agricultural and irrigation-infrastructure impacts.
COEN-INDECI reports increased Rio Pisco flow followed by erosion of the right bank that damaged the potable-water network in Tambo Colorado.
confirmed_positive_outcomes.mechanism_caution: This is a fluvial-erosion impact associated with increased river flow and is not relabeled as a river-overflow outcome.

negative_control_status.rule: No absence-of-report or non-damage day is promoted to a hydrologic negative without independent hydrometeorological and outcome adjudication.

scientific_limits: No event-paired primary rainfall or discharge series is ingested for the 2023-2024 Humay impact outcomes.

Letrayoc is retained as official upstream hydrologic monitoring context; station state is not transferred to Humay impact reaches without validated travel time, routing and receiving-channel capacity.
The 3-Mar-2024 Tambo Colorado record is fluvial erosion associated with increased Rio Pisco flow and is not relabeled as an overflow control.
San Andres canal-overflow evidence is a distinct local-drainage mechanism and is not used as Rio Pisco river-flood validation.
ANA 2025 critical-point work is current prevention/spatial context, not an observed 2023-2024 inundation footprint or historical hydraulic-capacity truth.
No confirmed negative control is fabricated.
No provider alert level, historical flow, design value or inferred discharge is promoted into an IRFEN operational threshold.
accepted_research_uses: bounded Rio Pisco historical positive-outcome validation
mechanism-separated river overflow and fluvial-erosion chronology
current official critical-point and prevention context
forbidden_uses: treating current critical-point work as historical event footprint
treating San Andres canal overflow as Rio Pisco river overflow
approving or activating the full Pisco-San Andres Phase-2 contract
